figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Basic aromatic frameworks of type II polyketides. Fasamycin (FAS) features an axial chiral framework that distinguishes it from the
others.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Biosynthetic gene cluster and the proposed biosynthetic pathway of fasamycin (FAS). (A) The biosynthetic gene cluster of FAS from S.
kanamyceticus CGMCC 4.1441.12 (B) The proposed biosynthetic pathway of FAS was analyzed as well as the FAS-derived products. Sp. indicates
spontaneous.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Characterization of FasU and its substrate 1. (A) UPLC analysis of the enzymatic reactions for FasU, FasR, and FasS as well as the
optimization of the reaction conditions (detection wavelength λ = 365 nm) using a Shim-pack XR-ODS III C18 column (75 × 2.0 mm, 1.6 μm).
(I−III) Assessment of the activity of FasU, FasS, or FasR on PDA. (IV−VI) Optimization of the 1-producing enzymatic reaction, with pH and
temperature selectively adjusted as indicated in each trace. (B) UPLC analysis of the enzymatic reactions for FasU using a Dikma Endeavorsil C18
column (100 × 2.1 mm, 1.8 μm; detection wavelength λ = 365 nm). (I) The 1-producing reaction. (II) Assessment of the activity of FasU by
adding it to the 1-producing enzymatic reaction. (III) Purified 1. (IV) Assessment of the activity of FasU using purified 1. (V, VI) FAS standard
and PDA standard. (C) UPLC analysis of the biosynthesis of FAS in S. coelicolor M1154 using a Shim-pack XR-ODS III C18 column (75 × 2.0
mm, 1.6 μm; detection wavelength λ = 365 nm). Sp. indicates spontaneous. (I) M1154 with fasU-integrated pJTU103, which harbors the
biosynthetic genes responsible for 1 biosynthesis. (II) M1154 with pJTU103. (III) M1154 wide-type strain (control). (D) HR-MS analysis of PDA
(observed 475.1400, calcd 475.1398) and 1 (observed 519.1298, calcd 519.1297), produced by the in vitro enzymatic reaction using 12C-malonyl-
CoA (MCoA) or 13C-MCoA as substrates. (E) The 13C NMR spectra for 1 (maroon) labeled by [1,2,3-13C3] MCoA and the 13C NMR spectra for
PDA (teal). C1 is the carboxyl group in 1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Analysis of the crystal structures of FasU and its substrate binding and catalytic mechanism. (A) The apo structure of FasU (PDB 9LSD).
The two monomeric FasU are colored in deep teal and wheat, respectively. (B) Surface representation showing the overall structure of the FasU
dimer with the same orientation and color scheme as in panel A. (C) FasU docking with 1 (optimized by MD simulation). Hydrogen bonds
between residues and hydroxyl groups of the substrate are indicated by dark dashed lines within 3.5 Å. The water molecule is shown in red. (D)
The binding conformation of the D-ring in 1. The carbon numbering (blue) of compound 1 (yellow) refers to Figure 2B. The hydrophobic
residues surrounding the D-ring are highlighted in deep teal. Surface (white) display of the active pocket of FasU. (E) The proposed catalytic
mechanisms for the FasU-mediated decarboxylation and cyclization in FAS biosynthesis (only the E-rings are shown).
